parts.text:
You are working for a client on a new software service. Nobody has designed it yet.

The client writes:

> Our customer companies need a new service for running their drone fleets from day to day, on our platform. Write the requirements for it: what the service must do, so that a team can build it and anyone can check whether it does.

What you know about the client's business:

A platform company runs a shared service for several independent drone operating companies. Its customers today include a parcel delivery firm, an infrastructure inspection firm, and a regional hospital logistics firm. Others are expected to join.

The customer companies compete with each other or work for clients who do. Each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business. They accept sharing airspace information, because that information comes from the authorities and is the same for everyone.

The people who will use the service work in three roles: fleet technician, dispatcher, airspace desk. You can reach one person in each role. A message that is exactly one line, `ASK <role>: <question>`, with `<role>` one of `technician`, `dispatcher` or `desk`, goes to that person, and their answer comes back to you. Each of them remembers what you asked them before. You can send at most 90 such questions in all. Any other message is taken as your requirements, and ends the work.

Write the requirements as a list in YAML, in exactly this format, with nothing else in that message:

```yaml
- id: DR-01
  requirement: >
    one thing the service must do, or must not do, and in which case
- id: DR-02
  requirement: >
    ...
```

Number the items DR-01, DR-02, and so on. Each item states one requirement in plain words.
Begin.
ASK technician: What are your primary responsibilities and what tasks do you need the service to support for day-to-day drone fleet maintenance?

My responsibilities are keeping the drones and charging equipment in working order. I add new drones to the fleet, retire old ones, set up charging pads at our sites, and take drones out of service for repairs and put them back. I also send drones to charge. Regulators can ask us to show how our drones have been looked after.
ASK technician: What specific details must be recorded for each drone, charging pad, maintenance activity, and regulatory compliance check?
I don't know.
ASK technician: When you add a drone to the fleet, what information do you enter about it? And what status can a drone have?
I don't know.
ASK technician: How do you take a drone out of service for repairs, put it back, and record how drones have been looked after for regulators?

I take drones out of service for repairs and put them back. Regulators can ask us to show how our drones have been looked after, and repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. I don't know how I record those things.
ASK dispatcher: What are your primary responsibilities and what tasks do you need the service to perform day-to-day?

As a dispatcher, I am the licensed person responsible for each flight, which means I decide which drone flies and along which way, and I sign off a flight before it leaves. I can also call off a flight. I need help finding out which of our drones could get to where a job starts, since software never chooses a drone or a way for us.
ASK desk: What are your primary responsibilities and what tasks do you need the service to perform day-to-day?

I keep the shared picture of the airspace, which includes the network of flight corridors between sites, the zones that group them, and the closures announced by the authorities. When a closure is entered, I want to know how much disruption it caused across customers. I work for all customer companies and have no business looking into any one company's operations.
ASK dispatcher: What information do you see or need to sign off a flight, choose a route/way, or find drones that can reach a job?
I don't know.
ASK dispatcher: When you plan or sign off a flight, what conditions or rules must be met before a flight can leave, and what does the system do if airspace closes?
I don't know.
ASK desk: What specific information is maintained for flight corridors, zones, and authority closures, and how is disruption measured across customers?
I don't know.
ASK technician: Can a technician from one company see or modify the fleet, charging pads, or maintenance records of another company?
Each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business. Our charging pads are never lent to another company.
ASK dispatcher: Can a dispatcher see or access jobs, drones, or flights of other companies, and what can you see about the shared airspace?

Each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business, so we do not see those of other companies. We accept sharing airspace information because that information comes from the authorities and is the same for everyone.
ASK desk: What happens when you enter an authority closure, and what does the airspace desk see about customer operations?
When I enter a closure, I want to know how much disruption it caused across customers. The airspace desk has no business looking into any one company's operations.
ASK dispatcher: What does the service do to help you find out which drones could get to where a job starts?
I don't know.
ASK desk: How should the service report or calculate disruption caused across customers without showing company-specific operations?
I don't know.
ASK dispatcher: What stages or statuses does a flight go through from creation to completion?
I don't know.
ASK technician: What can you tell me about sites and charging pads?
Each of our company's sites has a few dozen of our own charging pads, and each drone has a home site. We set up these charging pads at our sites, but our pads are never lent to another company.
ASK dispatcher: When you say software never chooses a drone or a way for us, what role does the service play in flight planning?
I don't know.
ASK desk: Can you add, modify, or remove flight corridors, zones, and closures?

I keep the shared picture of the airspace, which includes the network of flight corridors between sites, the zones that group them, and the closures announced by the authorities. Closures are often amended during the day, for example when an area is widened or an end time moves.
ASK technician: Does a drone have to be at a charging pad to charge, and can multiple drones use the same pad at the same time?
I don't know.
ASK technician: What happens when a drone is taken out of service, and can it fly while out of service?
I take drones out of service for repairs and put them back. My notes do not say whether a drone can fly while it is out of service.
ASK dispatcher: Can a drone fly if it is out of service or currently charging?
I don't know.
ASK dispatcher: What actions can a dispatcher perform on a flight?
As a dispatcher, I decide which drone flies and along which way, and I sign off a flight before it leaves. I can also call off a flight.
ASK desk: What happens to flight corridors when an authority announces a closure in a zone or area?
I don't know.
ASK technician: Does the service need to keep a maintenance history for regulators showing how drones have been looked after?

Repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians, and regulators can ask a company to show how its drones have been looked after. I don't know whether the service needs to keep a maintenance history for that purpose.
ASK technician: Can anyone other than a technician manage drones, charging pads, or repairs?

Repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians, and I keep drones and charging equipment in working order by adding new drones, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads, and taking drones out of service for repairs and putting them back. My notes do not state whether anyone other than a technician can manage these tasks.
